source_text: In Indian contexts, particularly within the Dawoodi Bohra community—a Shia Muslim sect with approximately one million members in India—the practice is commonly termed khatna, khafz, or khafd, referring to a ritual procedure involving the removal or nicking of the clitoral prepuce for purposes of religious purity and tradition, rather than intentional harm or disfigurement.
